TREASURY CASH FALLS $13.5B IN A DAY
The U.S. Treasury's cash account at the Federal Reserve, the TGA, fell $13.5 billion to $922.8 billion on November 5, according to the Daily Treasury Statement. The biggest outflow of the day was $4.9 billion in Medicaid grants. Money leaving https://t.co/yfW5fi1k3Q

Treasury's cash drawdown helped ease the drain on dollar funding. Bank reserves rose $67.6 billion in the week to November 4 as the government's balance at the Fed fell $79.4 billion.

The Fed's November 5 release puts Treasury cash at $936.2 billion and bank reserves at $2.963 https://t.co/udGs5ZibMn
$PSYC.CN (Psyched Wellness) enters a US$134,000 secured term loan with Gotham Green Funds. Interest at SOFR + 5%, maturing Nov 2028. Proceeds are for operating expenses and inventory.

After 165K October payrolls, fixing a floating-rate loan for two years costs roughly 58bp of carry on day one. The 2-year Treasury traded up to 4.52% after the report, per https://t.co/uUW97BOJfi, against SOFR of 3.94% on Nov 4.

The Treasury par close for the 2-year Thursday was https://t.co/5Xl9oXoAX0

The Treasury spends by drawing on its TGA balance. It can’t overdraw the TGA. Nor can the Fed directly credit it. The Fed can only create reserves. To convert reserves into TGA balances the Treasury either taxes or borrows. Therefore gov’t spending requires taxing or borrowing. https://t.co/QM8gpt4nQz
